item.text: The current settings have idle locking disabled: idle delay is `0` and screen lock is `false`. I’m setting a 5-minute idle timeout with immediate lock once the screen blanks.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc 'gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay 300 && gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled true && gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-delay 0 && gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay && gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled && gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-delay'

item.text: The lock settings are now applied and verified. I’m doing one extra compatibility check for the suspend-lock setting, since GNOME/Ubuntu versions differ slightly there.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc 'gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.screensaver ubuntu-lock-on-suspend true && gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver ubuntu-lock-on-suspend'
/bin/bash -lc 'gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.screensaver ubuntu-lock-on-suspend true && gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver ubuntu-lock-on-suspend'

item.text:
Done. Your computer is now set to lock automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity, and it will lock immediately when the screen blanks. It will also lock after suspend.

Verified settings:
`idle-delay = 300`
`lock-enabled = true`
`lock-delay = 0`
`ubuntu-lock-on-suspend = true`

I also noticed the root disk is nearly full, with about 583 MB free. That low-space warning is unrelated to locking, but it should be cleaned up soon.
